state.issue:
yq: navigating after a write (`.a.b = "y" | .a`) drops every comment, anchor and style the write did not touch

## Summary

When a pipe writes to the document and then *navigates* into it, the result loses every piece of presentation the write did not touch: trailing comments, anchors, quoting style. Real yq keeps them.

```
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x # c\n  d: &z "q"\n' | yq '.a.b = "y" | .a'
b: y # c
d: &z "q"
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x # c\n  d: &z "q"\n' | succinctly yq '.a.b = "y" | .a'
b: y
d: q
```

The same happens after `|=` and after a #798 metadata write, which makes the metadata write itself vanish:

```
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x\n' | yq '.a.b style = "double" | .a'
b: "x"
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.b style = "double" | .a'
b: x
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`evaluate_yaml_cursor` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) only builds the pristine `CommentTree` snapshot and reconciles presentation when `is_alias_sensitive_assign(expr)` holds, and that predicate's `is_shape_preserving` half returns `false` for a trailing navigation stage. So the result value is a plain `OwnedValue` with an empty tree: no comment, anchor or style survives, and the #798 write pass never runs at all (it is gated on the same `presentation_sync_ctx`).

This is not specific to #798. It is the same hole for every write form, which is why the review fix for #798 documented it under "Three known gaps this write shares with every other write form" in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` rather than erroring.

## Possible direction

Let `is_shape_preserving` admit a *trailing* static-navigation suffix (`.a`, `.a.b`, `.a[0]`) after a shape-preserving prefix, and have the reconcile step navigate the pristine tree by the same steps so the result's subtree keeps its metadata. `static_nav_steps` already exists for exactly this kind of path. A non-static trailing navigation (`.[]`, `.[(.i)]`) can stay unsupported.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #1349 (a multi-result filter carries no `CommentTree` at all), which is the other route that drops all presentation.
